canonical_topic: Wait times and timeliness of care
description: The perceived speed of the care process from arrival to discharge or admission, including waiting times in emergency departments, urgent care, outpatient clinics, and for scheduled appointments. Captures triage throughput, boarding delays, and overall patient flow efficiency, whether fast or slow.

canonical_topic: Front desk, reception and administrative staff conduct
description: Interpersonal conduct of non-clinical front-line staff (receptionists, registration/check-in clerks, administrative/office staff): rudeness, dismissiveness, attitude and unhelpfulness — as well as courtesy — at arrival and administrative contact.

canonical_topic: Clinical staff bedside manner and empathy
description: Interpersonal conduct of clinical staff (doctors, nurses, technicians): friendliness, empathy, respect, listening, compassion, professionalism, rudeness and dismissiveness during care. Excludes security and front-desk staff.

Exchange of information between staff and patients/families during and after visits, including clinical updates, explanations of conditions and tests, test result communication, callbacks, and clarity/consistency of messages.
Accuracy and transparency of charges: overbilling, surprise or unexpected charges, duplicate/incorrect billing, disputes, payment processing and collections.

canonical_topic: Insurance coverage, denials and network issues
description: Insurance-related experiences: coverage verification, claim denials, out-of-network and authorization problems, and care refused or delayed due to insurance or eligibility.
Visible cleanliness, sanitation, and housekeeping of patient rooms, bathrooms, waiting areas, and facilities, including odors and overall tidiness.

canonical_topic: Infection control and health safety practices
description: Measures to prevent infection and maintain a safe clinical environment, including mask requirements, COVID-19 testing at entry, isolation protocols, and protective equipment use.
Non-clinical amenities and logistics: food and meal service, parking, wayfinding/signage, and comfort amenities during visits and stays.

Physical condition and comfort of the facility: room and common-area maintenance, cleanliness mentions, noise, temperature and general environment. (Overlaps with the separate 'Cleanliness and housekeeping' topic.)
Adequacy and timeliness of pain relief: whether patients' pain was taken seriously, treated promptly, and controlled effectively during and after care.
Prescribing, dispensing, administration, refills and pharmacy coordination: medication errors, missing or wrong medications, prescription and refill delays. Excludes pain-relief adequacy.
Thoroughness of medical evaluations, correctness of diagnoses, ordering of appropriate examinations and tests, and clinical decision-making, including the extent of physician involvement.
Preventable adverse events, medical errors, procedural mishaps, neglect, falls, infections, and lapses in clinical or procedural safety that risk patient harm.

Experiences with ordering, scheduling, undergoing, and receiving results from laboratory tests, imaging studies (CT, MRI, X-ray), and other diagnostics, including equipment availability and testing turnaround times.

canonical_topic: Nursing responsiveness and basic care needs
description: Timeliness and adequacy of nursing staff response to call buttons, requests for assistance, and basic personal care needs such as toileting, positioning, and comfort measures during a stay.
Adequacy of staffing numbers, facility capacity, and resources such as beds and equipment, and the impact of understaffing or overcrowding on care delivery.
Experiences related to leaving the facility, including timeliness of discharge, clarity and completeness of instructions, paperwork handling, and immediate follow-up arrangements.
Continuity of care across providers and settings, including referrals to specialists, transfers between facilities, internal handoffs, and management of follow-up care after a visit.
Protection of personal health information, physical privacy during exams and discussions, HIPAA compliance, and prevention of unauthorized disclosure.

canonical_topic: Visitor access, security, and property safety
description: Policies and enforcement regarding visitors and family presence, interactions with security personnel, and safety of personal belongings on-site.
Perceptions of biased or unfair treatment based on race, ethnicity, language, disability, gender identity, or other personal characteristics, and the overall equity of care delivery.
Quality, safety, and environment of inpatient and outpatient psychiatric, mental health, and substance use treatment, including staff interactions, treatment approaches, and patient rights.
Care experiences for pregnant women, newborns, children, and adolescents, including labor and delivery, NICU, pediatric emergency visits, and family-inclusive treatment.
Experiences with operative and invasive procedures, including pre-operative preparation, anesthesia, surgical quality, post-operative recovery, and related communication.

canonical_topic: Rehabilitation and long-term care / therapy services
description: Quality and availability of physical, occupational, and speech therapy, as well as care in inpatient rehabilitation facilities, skilled nursing units, and long-term acute care settings.
Ability to obtain, reschedule, and cancel appointments, ease of reaching the facility by phone or online for scheduling, and the overall accessibility of non-emergency care.
Accuracy and availability of medical records, charts, and administrative paperwork, including errors, access requests, and health information management.
Availability and quality of physical accessibility (wheelchair access, ramps), mobility support, and communication accommodations including language interpretation and aids for sensory disabilities.
